issues.title: [Bug] FP8 KV cache scales are silently dropped when loading Qwen3-MoE / Qwen2 / Mixtral and every layer falls back to scale 1.0
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When a checkpoint carries FP8 KV cache scales as tensors, the hand-written weight loaders of `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, and `MixtralForCausalLM` drop them. `process_weights_after_loading` then sees both scales still at their initial -1.0 and resets them to 1.0.

```python
# python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/kv_cache.py, current main
elif layer.k_scale <= 0.0 and layer.v_scale <= 0.0:
    # If no scales were loaded (both scales are invalid non-positive
    # values), use the default value of 1.0
    k_scale = 1.0
    v_scale = 1.0
```

Every attention layer therefore dequantizes its FP8 cache with a unit scale, and the per-layer error equals the calibrated scale. Outputs stay finite, nothing is raised, and the error is invisible to tensor-level checks.

Three scale namings are affected. llm-compressor stores the scales under the fused projection name, for example `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale` (the layout reported in vllm-project/vllm#25047). ModelOpt stores them per projection, for example `model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale`. The deprecated single `.kv_scale` tensor is lost as well, while the model registers the scales at `self_attn.attn.k_scale` and `self_attn.attn.v_scale`.

### Mechanism

The loaders run their `stacked_params_mapping` loop before the params lookup, and the mapping is a substring replace.

```python
# python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py, current main
for param_name, weight_name, shard_id in stacked_params_mapping:   # 1186
    if weight_name not in name:
        continue
    ...
    name = name.replace(weight_name, param_name)                   # 1198
    ...
    if name not in params_dict:                                    # 1202
        continue
```

`"v_proj"` is a substring of `"qkv_proj"`, so the fused scale name becomes the nonexistent `self_attn.qkqkv_proj.k_scale`. The per-projection name is rewritten into `self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale`, which does not exist either because the model keeps the scales on `self_attn.attn`.

| model file                                       | fused naming                       | per-projection naming            | deprecated `.kv_scale` |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `qwen3_moe.py`                                   | dropped, 0 warnings                | dropped, 0 warnings              | dropped, 0 warnings    |
| `qwen2.py` (default `_legacy_load_weights` path) | dropped, 2 "not found" warnings    | dropped, 2 warnings              | dropped, 1 warning     |
| `mixtral.py`                                     | `KeyError` on `qkqkv_proj.k_scale` | `KeyError` on `qkv_proj.k_scale` | silently skipped       |

The dangerous row is qwen3_moe, whose whole path from loading to the 1.0 fallback prints nothing at all. vllm had the same defect in vllm-project/vllm#25047 and at least logged a startup warning there ("Using KV cache scaling factor 1.0 ..."), which is how that issue was noticed. The per-projection layout is the fully silent real-world path, because its `k_proj.weight` / `v_proj.weight` tensors load correctly through the same stacked mapping and the loss touches only the scale tensors.

### Scope and fix shape

sglang already has the bridge for this naming gap. `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` in `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py` remaps ModelOpt and deprecated names, and 30 model files

issues.title: [Tracking] Pipeline parallelism x speculative decoding (EAGLE/MTP): converge prefill gate PRs, make the path model-agnostic, decide decode design
issues.body:
## Motivation

Pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding are still gated off against each other, but the pieces to lift the gate have been landing and are now in flight from several authors with overlapping scope. This issue tracks the work so the remaining PRs can converge on one design instead of a per-model allowlist.

Concrete use case: PD-disaggregated serving of large hybrid MoE models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 / DeepSeek / GLM) where the prefill role runs PP (e.g. PP4 for the InferenceMAX AgentX recipe) and the decode role uses MTP. Today the prefill role only starts with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1` to skip the assertion, or with one of the model-specific gate PRs below.

## What is already model-agnostic (merged)

Since #35758 the prefill-side runtime does not depend on the model:

- The draft worker is created only on the last PP stage (`EAGLEWorkerV2._hosts_draft`); other stages return proxy tensors so scheduler dispatch stays rank-uniform.
- `scheduler_pp_mixin` carries the draft output (`draft_topk_p`, `draft_topk_index`, `draft_hidden_states`) along the PP ring and rebinds it as `batch.spec_info` on stage 0 so the PD result contains it.

## What is still model-specific today

**1. Last-stage draft embedding (the only hard dependency).** `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` calls `target.get_embed_and_head()`. On the last stage `embed_tokens` is a `PPMissingLayer` for most targets (`deepseek_v2`, `llama`, `glm4_moe`, ...), so `.weight` raises. Two different fixes exist:

- Qwen3.5 (#37471, merged): the draft keeps its own embedding and `qwen3_5_mtp.load_weights` loads it from the target checkpoint; the target returns `embed=None` on non-first stages.
- DeepSeek / GLM (#39378, open): the target materializes `embed_tokens` on the last stage (`pp_stage_needs_embedding`) and the draft borrows it.

Every new model currently has to pick one and re-implement it in its own model file. The allowlists in #39378 / #39602 / #38698 exist only to express "this model did that work".

**2. Extra `spec_info` fields on the ring.** The ring serializes three hard-coded tensors. DSA models need `draft_dsa_topk_indices` (added by hand in #39378); the next model with extra draft state will need another hand-written field.

**3. EAGLE3 / DFLASH aux-hidden capture is silently disabled under PP.** `set_eagle3_layers_to_capture` / `set_dflash_layers_to_capture` return early on non-last ranks, so capture layers that live on earlier stages are never captured. Affects Llama / gpt-oss / Kimi-K2.5 EAGLE3 drafts. This is a correctness gap, not a gate.

**4. Targets without PP at all.** `qwen3_next.py`, `longcat_flash.py`, `hunyuan_v4.py` have no PP support in the target; PP+MTP is moot there until PP lands.

**5. PD KV transfer under PP** for non-standard pools is being fixed per pool: MLA layer offsets in nixl (#39378), hybrid mamba pools (#33584), QSA / PLE pools (#38698). PP is only permitted on the disagg prefill role, so these block the actual use case.

## Status by model family

| Family | Target PP | Draft embedding on last stage | Ring fields | PD KV under PP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5 | yes | yes (#37471) | ok | hybrid pool: #33584 |
| DeepSeek V3 / V3.2, GLM-5 | yes | #39378 | DSA: #39378 | MLA: #39378 |
| Qwen3.8 / Qwen4Exp | #38698 | #38698 | ok | QSA/PLE: #38698 |
| Llama / gpt-oss EAGLE3 | yes | missing | ok | ok | 
| Qwen3-Next, LongCat-Flash, Hunyuan-v4 | missing | missing | missing | missing |

## In-flight PRs

Prefill gate (overlapping):
- #39378

issues.title: [Feature] Reduce constrained-decoding overhead in TP
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

Currently, when tensor-parallelism (TP) and constrained-decoding are enabled, each TP worker will compile the same grammar across different TP ranks. This will incur non-trivial CPU overhead (for TP $n$, the overhead is $n \times$. In fact, we only need to compile the grammar and sample the result on the first rank.

A possible implementation can be:

1. Only apply grammar token mask on the rank 0.
2. Broadcast the next tokens id from rank 0 when there're grammars in batch.
3. Keep the old code path when there's no grammar in batch (i.e. no extra all-reduce).

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5c2915494c83f076a11afb2c3382eeb8a41f1974/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L205-L217

issues.title: [Feature] Unified JIT / Precompilation Cache Directory
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation


## Summary

**Request:** Unify all JIT and precompilation cache paths under a single configurable root so that users and operators can manage cache location, size, and persistence in one place. The current situation is fragmented across multiple env vars and default paths (including `/tmp`), which makes it hard to reason about where compiled artifacts live and to reuse caches across runs or machines.

## Current State (Fragmented)

### 1. Triton JIT cache

| What | Env var / source | Default / behavior |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| Direct `@triton.jit` (e.g. allocator, MoE kernels) | `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` (Triton runtime) | Triton default: `~/.triton/cache`; often overwritten by Inductor to a path under `/tmp/torchinductor_*` |
| SGLang override | `SGLANG_TRITON_CACHE_DIR` (if implemented) | e.g. `~/.triton/cache` or `~/.cache/triton` |

- Set only in some entry paths (engine, gRPC launcher, scheduler process); custom/PD launchers may not set it.
- When PyTorch Inductor runs first, it can set `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` to its own subdir, so later Triton JIT (including allocator) writes under `/tmp`.

### 2. PyTorch Inductor (torch.compile)

| What | Env var / source | Default / behavior |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| Inductor cache | `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` (PyTorch) | `/tmp/torchinductor_<user>` (or similar) |
| SGLang override | `SGLANG_TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` (if implemented) | e.g. `~/.cache/sglang/inductor` |

- Default lives in `/tmp`, so cache is often non-persistent and can conflict with other users on shared nodes.

### 3. DeepGEMM JIT cache

| What | Env var / source | Default / behavior |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| DeepGEMM cache | `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR` / `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` | `~/.cache/deep_gemm` |

- Set in `layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py`; separate from Triton/Inductor.
- 
## Problems

1. **No single root:** Triton, Inductor, SGLang torch_compile, and DeepGEMM each have their own env or default; some write to `/tmp`, others to `~/.cache/...`.

## Proposal

### 1. Introduce a single JIT cache root

- **New env var:** `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT` (or `SGLANG_CACHE_ROOT` if we want to align with existing `SGLANG_CACHE_ROOT` in custom_all_reduce_utils).
- **Default:** `~/.cache/sglang` (or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/sglang` when set).
- **Semantics:** All JIT/precompilation caches that SGLang controls should live under this root in fixed subdirs.

### 2. Standard layout under the root

Suggested subdirs (all under `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT`):

| Subdir | Purpose | Maps from |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| `triton/` | Triton JIT (direct `@triton.jit` and, when possible, Triton used by Inductor) | `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` |
| `inductor/` | PyTorch Inductor (torch.compile) | `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` |
| `torch_compile/` | SGLang torch.compile cache (hash-based, when using SGLangBackend) | `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` + `torch_compile_cache` |
| `deep_gemm/` | DeepGEMM JIT | `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR` / `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` |

- If we keep backward compatibility, existing env vars (`SGLANG_TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`) could override the default subdir path when set; otherw

issues.title: [Roadmap] sglang auto tuner
issues.body:
Now we have many kernel backends for moe (e.g., triton, cutlass), attention, and allreduce. For each kernel, we can also tune some configs (e.g., the tile sizes in triton fused moe). Tuning these kernels and choosing dispatching heuristics can be non-trivial. We would like to build a simple command that auto-tune all the kernels and dispatch heuristic for a model.

## Todo
1. Implement a script sglang.auto_tune to tune the kernels and hyperparameters for a specific model. It should dump the optimal tile sizes/dispatching heuristics for all kernels used in this model. Example usage:
    - `python3 -m sglang.auto_tune --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 8`
    - `python3 -m sglang.auto_tune --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 4`
2. Start from tuning the triton fused moe https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton
3. Implement a github action workflow that tunes 20 popular models on 5 common platforms.
    - The workflow should take in two arguments: a list of model names, and a list of runner names
    - Our CI has H100, H20, H200, B200, GB200
4. Auto choose allreduce algorithms (custom allreduce, nccl, nccl symmetric memory, torch symmetric memory).
5. Auto choose attention kernel backend and moe runner backend.
6. Auto tune the cutlass gemm kernels (with cutlass profiler)
7. Auto choose speculative decoding parameters for different batch sizes.

issues.title: [Feature] support `gather` instead of `all_gather` when gathering the logits
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation

We noticed that in the `_get_logits` function of vllm, `gather` instead of `all_gather` will be used under certain conditions (the main condition is that for non-tpu devices):
Code link:

- [logits = tensor_model_parallel_gather(logits)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e1fc61f0fb90c37f0d4a1a8f76235a6e4e1103c/vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py#L101C22-L101C50)

- [condition of whether using `all_gather` or `gather`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e1fc61f0fb90c37f0d4a1a8f76235a6e4e1103c/vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py#L53-L57)

The change from using `all_gather` to `gather` is initially added in this PR for your reference: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/2221.

While in SGLang, we see currently `all_gather` is always used:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e868d0b60eb2d435c5599165f787bca06bdc9c3d/python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py#L246

Does SGLang have the plan to add `gather` instead of only `all_gather` when gathering the logits? Per the practice in vllm, using `gather` seems to have better performance than `all_gather` on devices which have `gather` support.

issues.title: [Feature] Support piggyback server load report.
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation

To support a flexible and reliable load balancing strategy, external router (sgl-router) and internal controller (dp-controller) should be aware of the real-time load situation.

Current implementation uses a polling mechanism and a watch-based communicator to query load from the scheduler. However, this is flexible and elegant.

- Implement a piggyback load reporting mechanism, in which load information is carried through restreaming token messages.
- Also keep the watching mode, always storing the latest load information in http worker for external query.

tasks.why_core: 掌握 Omni 框架的生命周期管理和显存统筹，是成为端侧多模态系统底层架构负责人的必经之路。
tasks.goal: 为 Omni stages（如 ASR）实现 `release_memory_occupation` 和 `resume_memory_occupation` API，使其在空闲时释放显存。
tasks.first_action: 调查 `sglang_omni` 的 HTTP server 路由，了解如何将请求传递给 stage worker 进程。
implementation_steps: 在 Omni HTTP server 中添加 `/release_memory_occupation` 和 `/resume_memory_occupation` 路由。
实现与 stage worker 进程的通信机制，传递释放/恢复指令。
在 stage worker 中调用底层的 SGLang memory saver 逻辑。
修复 `LD_PRELOAD` 相关的子进程环境变量问题。
validation: 在 Mac 上启动一个轻量级模型（如 Qwen3-ASR MLX），调用 API 并观察内存占用变化。
questions: Omni-native admin API 的具体设计规范是什么？是否需要支持细粒度的 tags（如 weights, kv_cache）？
risks: 多进程环境下的状态同步问题；MLX 后端对内存释放的支持可能与 CUDA 不同，需要做适配或 Fallback。
tasks.skill_fit: 显存管理与系统级调度逻辑。
tasks.engagement: Issue 开放且无 assignee，无 linked PRs，非常适合直接认领。
tasks.claim_comment: Hi, I'd like to work on this. Since I'm developing on an Apple Silicon Mac, I plan to implement the Omni-native admin API for memory management and test it with the MLX backend first. Could you confirm if the API should exactly match the upstream SGLang signature, or if a simplified version is preferred for Omni stages? I can submit a draft PR in 3-4 days.
tasks.pr_scope: 实现基础的 HTTP 路由和进程间通信指令，先不处理复杂的 `LD_PRELOAD` 修复。

positioning.overview: SGLang-Omni 是一个专为全模态（Omni）和音频（TTS/ASR）模型设计的高性能服务框架。与传统的纯文本大语言模型（LLM）推理框架不同，全模态和语音生成任务具有显著的多阶段（Multi-stage）特征。例如，一个语音对话请求需要经过预处理、音频编码、自回归语言模型解码、DiT或Vocoder声码器生成等多个异构计算阶段。这些阶段的计算模式、显存需求和依赖关系截然不同。SGLang-Omni 的核心价值在于它在底层 SGLang 的自回归引擎之上，构建了一套完整的流水线拓扑（Pipeline Topology）、阶段专属调度器（Stage-specialized scheduling）以及跨阶段的传输数据面（基于共享内存、ZMQ、NCCL、NIXL 和 Mooncake）。对于你这位资深性能工程师而言，虽然目前受限于只有一台 16GB 的 MacBook Air，但这恰好与该项目当前大力发展的 Apple Silicon (MLX/MPS) 生态完美契合。证据表明，项目在 pyproject.toml 中专门为 darwin 和 arm64 平台配置了 mlx 和 mlx-lm 依赖，并且最近的提交热点高度集中在 OmniTyper（一个基于 MLX 的 macOS 原生流式 ASR 客户端）。此外，项目原生支持 MiniMax Music 3 等基于 DiT（Diffusion Transformer）的音乐生成模型（依赖 cache-dit）。你可以利用你在 DiT 推理加速和算子融合方面的深厚积累，在本地通过 MLX/MPS 开发和验证 DiT 算子或流水线调度优化，最后利用 Colab T4 进行 CUDA 相关的快速回归测试。该项目目前处于 v0.1.6 的早期高速迭代阶段，架构设计极具前瞻性，是切入多模态系统底层架构的绝佳标的。
positioning.problem: 解决多模态和语音模型在生产环境中端到端推理效率低下的问题。传统的 LLM 框架无法高效处理流式音频的声码器调度，也缺乏对 DiT 等扩散模型与自回归模型混合流水线的原生支持，导致异构计算资源利用率低、跨阶段显存传输开销大。
positioning.users: 目标用户为 AI 基础设施工程师、多模态大模型研究员以及需要部署实时语音助手（如 Qwen3-Omni）、音乐生成（MiniMax Music 3）或高并发 TTS/ASR 服务的企业开发者。典型场景包括实时端到端语音对话、批量语音合成、流式语音识别以及基于文本和音频提示的复杂多模态生成。

landscape.difference: vLLM 专注于纯文本和视觉语言模型（VLM）的单阶段自回归推理，缺乏对音频声码器和多阶段异构流水线的原生调度支持。
本项目的底层依赖，专注于 RadixAttention 和自回归调度。Omni 在其之上扩展了音频处理、DiT集成和跨阶段传输（ZMQ/Mooncake）。
提供通用的 Ensemble 流水线，但配置繁琐且缺乏针对 LLM/DiT 混合架构的显存级零拷贝传输优化（如 Omni 使用的 Mooncake 和 NIXL）。

landscape.project: Fish Speech / CosyVoice 官方仓库
landscape.difference: 仅提供单机单卡的研究用途推理脚本，缺乏批处理、流式 API 和生产级调度。Omni 将它们统一纳入了高性能、OpenAI 兼容的服务框架。

positioning.stage: 处于早期但高速迭代的生产可用阶段（2026年9月发布 v0.1.6）。正在密集扩展硬件后端（Apple Silicon, XPU, MUSA）和接入最新全模态模型。

capabilities.capability: Multi-stage Pipeline Topology (多阶段流水线拓扑)
Stage-specialized Scheduling (阶段专属调度)
Inter-stage Transport & Relay (跨阶段传输与中继)
Apple Silicon / MLX Native Support (苹果芯片原生支持)
DiT / Music Generation Integration (DiT与音乐生成集成)
Omni Router (多节点路由与负载均衡)
OpenAI-compatible API (兼容OpenAI的API服务)
Native macOS Client (macOS原生流式客户端)

positioning.numbers: 核心代码 sglang_omni 包含 601 个文件，测试用例 512 个文件，文档 90 个文件。2026年9月内密集发布了 v0.1.4 到 v0.1.6 三个版本。最近提交热点高度集中在 OmniTyper (累计近50次变更) 和 sglang_omni/models (13次变更)。

codemap.layers:
SGLang-Omni 的架构设计高度契合多模态与语音任务的「多阶段（Multi-stage）」物理特性。对于你这位受限于 Apple Silicon 硬件但精通 DiT 与底层性能的专家，理解其分层逻辑是利用 MLX 开展本地研发的关键。

1. **接入与路由层 (Access & Routing)**：位于 `sglang_omni_router` 和 `sglang_omni/http`。负责处理 OpenAI 兼容的 REST API 和 WebSocket 流式请求。最近的高频热点 `OmniTyper`（macOS 原生客户端）正是通过 WebSocket 与此层交互，这是你在本地验证端到端流式 ASR/TTS 的最佳入口。

2. **流水线与调度层 (Pipeline & Scheduling)**：核心在 `sglang_omni/pipeline` 和 `sglang_omni/scheduling`。与纯 LLM 框架不同，Omni 将请求拆分为异构阶段（如 Pre-LM 编码、自回归解码、DiT 声码器生成）。`EngineBuilder`（如 `AsrEngineBuilder`）负责根据模型拓扑组装这些阶段，并为不同阶段分配专属调度策略（如音频 Patch 批处理 vs Token 批处理）。

3. **通信与数据面 (Communication & Data Plane)**：位于 `sglang_omni/comm`。解决跨阶段的 Tensor 传输问题。在多卡/多机环境下依赖 NCCL、NIXL 和 Mooncake（见 `pyproject.toml` 依赖）；但在你的 MacBook 上，它将回退到基于共享内存或本地 ZMQ 的传输，这部分逻辑在 `stage_io.py` 中。

4. **执行与模型层 (Execution & Models)**：位于 `sglang_omni/model_runner` 和 `sglang_omni/models`。这是你的主战场。框架复用了底层 SGLang 的自回归能力，但通过 `ModelRunner` 暴露了 `before_prefill` 和 `before_decode` 钩子，用于注入音频特征或处理连续潜变量（Latents）。模型目录下包含了大量 DiT/Flow Matching 实现（如 `minimax_music3`、`fun_cosyvoice3`、`auk`）。

5. **硬件与 Kernel 层 (Hardware & Kernel)**：位于 `sglang_omni/platforms` 和各模型的 `mlx` 子目录。项目通过 `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` 环境变量和 `mlx-lm` 依赖原生支持 Apple Silicon。你可以在这里开发 MLX 版本的 DiT 算子融合，最后再通过 Colab T4 编写对应的 CUDA/Triton 版本（如 `fused_qk_norm_rope.py`）。

codemap.data_flow:
以一个典型的文本到语音（TTS）请求（例如使用基于 DiT 的 CosyVoice3 或 MiniMax Music 3）为例，数据在 SGLang-Omni 中的完整流转路径如下，这充分体现了其「多阶段流水线」的设计哲学：

1. **请求接入与解析 (Ingestion)**：客户端（如 OmniTyper 或 HTTP 客户端）发起 `/v1/audio/speech` 请求。请求首先到达 `sglang_omni/http` 或 `sglang_omni_router`。在这里，原始 JSON 被反序列化并校验，转换为内部的强类型数据结构（定义在各模型的 `payload_types.py` 中）。

2. **准入与路由 (Admission & Routing)**：`sglang_omni/admission.py` 接收请求，并根据 `config/topology.py` 中定义的流水线拓扑，决定该请求需要经历哪些计算阶段。对于 TTS，通常包括：文本预处理/特征提取 -> 自回归（AR）语义解码 -> DiT/Flow Matching 声码器生成。

3. **阶段一：预处理与特征提取 (Pre-LM)**：请求进入第一个 Worker。文本被 Tokenizer 处理，如果包含参考音频（Voice Cloning），则通过 `encoder_service.py`（如 `FunASRPreLMEncoderService`）提取声学特征。这些特征被打包进 `request_builders.py` 生成的内部请求对象中。

4. **阶段二：自回归语义解码 (AR Decode)**：请求被送入 SGLang 的核心调度器。此时，`sglang_omni/model_runner/base.py` 中的 `ModelRunner` 开始介入。在 `before_prefill` 阶段，Runner 将阶段一提取的特征注入到模型的 `input_embeds` 中。随后，底层引擎执行 Prefill 和 Decode。在 `before_decode` 和输出收集阶段（如 `fishaudio_s2_pro/model_runner.py` 中的 `collect_s2pro_step_outputs`），生成的语义 Token 或连续潜变量（Latents）被逐帧截获。

5. **跨阶段传输 (Inter-stage Transport)**：生成的语义 Latents 不能一直堆积在 AR 阶段的显存中。通过 `sglang_omni/comm/stage_io.py`，这些 Tensor 数据被异步发送到下一个阶段。在你的 MacBook 上，这通过共享内存或 ZMQ 完成；在生产环境的 GPU 集群上，则通过 NCCL 或 Mooncake 引擎实现零拷贝传输。

6. **阶段三：DiT / Vocoder 生成 (Acoustic Tail)**：这是你作为性能工程师最能发挥价值的阶段。接收到 Latents 后，后置阶段的调度器（如 `DotsTTSEngineBuilder` 配置的独立调度器）被唤醒。数据进入 `packed_dit.py` 或 `flow_matching.py`。在这里，常微分方程（ODE）求解器和 DiT 网络进行多次迭代，将 Latents 转换为高频音频波形。由于 DiT 的计算模式（固定步长、计算密集）与 AR（逐 Token、访存密集）完全不同，Omni 在这里使用了完全独立的 Batching 策略（如按 Audio Patches 批处理）。

7. **流式输出 (Streaming Output)**：生成的音频波形块（Chunks）通过 ZMQ 控制面传回 Router，最终通过 WebSocket 或 HTTP Chunked 编码实时流式推送给客户端，完成端到端生成。

key_types.name: AsrEngineBuilder / TtsEngineBuilder
key_types.purpose: 定义模型流水线拓扑的基类，控制并发上限、显存比例及是否启用 Pre-LM 阶段。

key_types.name: ModelRunner
key_types.purpose: 核心扩展点，提供 before_prefill 和 before_decode 钩子，用于在 SGLang 底层调度前后注入自定义逻辑。

key_types.name: NativeASRServer
key_types.purpose: 管理本地 MLX 语音模型的生命周期，是 macOS 原生客户端启动本地推理服务的入口。

key_types.name: DotsFlowStep
key_types.purpose: 定义 DiT/Flow Matching 的单步计算状态，用于在多阶段流水线中传递声码器上下文。

key_types.name: _DotsFlowLaunchBuf
key_types.purpose: 声学尾部（Acoustic-tail）的启动载荷数据结构，用于将 AR 阶段的输出打包发给 DiT 阶段。

key_types.name: FunASRPreLMEncoderService
key_types.purpose: 处理进入语言模型前的音频特征提取，支持 CUDA Graph 加速（需验证 MLX 下的回退逻辑）。

key_types.name: collect_s2pro_step_outputs
key_types.purpose: 在自回归 Decode 阶段收集语义 Token，并维护 Phase-aware 的历史状态（semantic_history_tokens）。

key_types.name: ArkasrEngineBuilder
key_types.purpose: ARK-ASR 的引擎构建器，展示了如何配置 pre_lm_cache_size_bytes 和异步解码参数。

extension_points.how: 在 `sglang_omni/models/` 下新建目录。必须实现继承自 `TtsEngineBuilder` 或 `AsrEngineBuilder` 的类，定义 `request_builders.py`（解析请求），并实现自定义的 `ModelRunner` 以处理特定的前向逻辑。

extension_points.where: 新后端支持 (如 MLX 深度优化)
extension_points.how: 在 `sglang_omni/model_runner/audio_mlx.py` 或具体模型的 `mlx/` 子目录（如 `fun_cosyvoice3/mlx/`）中添加逻辑。通过环境变量 `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` 触发，利用 Apple Silicon 的统一内存架构优化跨阶段传输。
在具体模型的算子文件中修改（如 `models/auk/fused_qk_norm_rope.py` 或 `models/minimax_music3/dit.py`）。你可以先在本地用 MLX 编写等效的 Python/C++ 算子验证数学正确性，随后在 Colab T4 上编写 Triton/CUDA 版本并挂载到 PyTorch 模块中。
修改 `sglang_omni/scheduling/` 下的策略文件（如 `generation_batch_policy.py`）。例如，针对 DiT 阶段实现基于 Sequence Length 的动态 Batching，需在 `EngineBuilder` 中注册新的 Policy。

hotspots.why: 近期提交极其密集（合计近 40 次）。项目正在大力发展基于 MLX 的 macOS 原生流式 ASR 客户端，修复了主线程卡顿、增加了无 API 听写模式等。这是你本地开发的最佳切入点。
近期有关于 `packed Flow sequence` 的核心优化提交（Read the packed Flow sequence ragged instead of padding）。这直接涉及 DiT 性能优化，与你的技能树完美匹配。
近期提交了性能优化（encode references on a separate CUDA stream），表明项目高度关注多阶段并发执行的底层流（Stream）调度。
高频修改（11次）。随着新模型（AuK, MiniMax）和新后端（XPU, MUSA）的加入，单元测试是保证流水线不被破坏的防线。你本地验证 MLX 逻辑也需重度依赖此目录。
近期增加了对 Intel XPU 和 MUSA（摩尔线程）设备路径的支持，说明框架的硬件抽象层正在快速演进，MLX 的支持逻辑也在此处维护。

runbook.no_gpu_paths:
在你的 Apple Silicon MacBook 上，你可以畅通无阻地执行和调试以下路径：1. `OmniTyper` 目录下的 macOS 原生客户端及 `OmniTyper/backend/server.py`（近期最高频提交热点，25次提交）；2. `sglang_omni/model_runner/audio_mlx.py` 和 `mlx_model_worker.py`（MLX 运行器）；3. `sglang_omni/models/fun_cosyvoice3/mlx/`（包含完整的 MLX 版 DiT、Vocoder 和 Flow Matching 实现）；4. `sglang_omni/model_runner/audio_torch_mps.py`（Torch MPS 后端）。

你只能阅读代码或必须依赖 Colab T4 验证的路径：1. `sglang_omni/models/fishaudio_s2_pro/`（其 `engine_builder.py` 强校验 SM89/90/100/120 及 FlashInfer，Mac 上会直接抛出 RuntimeError）；2. 所有 `*_cuda_graph.py` 文件（如 `arkasr/encoder_cuda_graph.py`、`minimax_music3/rvq_cuda_graph.py`）；3. `sglang_omni/comm/kv_transfer.py` 及依赖 `nixl-cu13` / `mooncake` 的多机多卡通信数据面。
runbook.test_suite: 测试框架推测为 `pytest`。测试目录集中在 `tests/unit_test`（近期提交热点，11次提交）和 `tests/test_model`。在 Mac 上，你需要通过目录隔离或 marker 过滤掉 CUDA 相关的测试（例如 `pytest tests/unit_test/ -k "not cuda"`，需验证具体 marker）。由于跳过了大模型加载和多卡通信，纯 CPU/MLX 的单元测试子集大概耗时在几分钟内。
debug_tips: 环境变量 `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` 是在 Mac 上激活 MLX 后端的总开关（见 `OmniTyper/backend/server.py`）。
环境变量 `SGLANG_OMNI_STRICT_PORT=1` 和 `SGLANG_OMNI_ADMIN_KEY` 用于本地调试 OmniTyper 后端时的端口和鉴权控制。
Profiling 入口位于 `sglang_omni/profiler/` 目录，以及专门针对 ASR 的 `benchmarks/eval/asr_profiling.py`。
日志系统基于标准 `logging`（代码中广泛使用 `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`），可通过修改 level 开启 Debug 日志。
runbook.ci: CI 基于 GitHub Actions（位于 `.github/workflows/`）。PR 会被严格的门禁脚本卡住，包括 `.github/scripts/pr_ci_gate.py` 和 `.github/scripts/verify_omni_installed_pins.py`。此外，文档明确指出提交 PR 前必须在本地运行 `pre-commit run --all-files`，否则代码风格（如 isort）或文档格式检查会导致 CI 失败。
pitfalls: 依赖陷阱：千万不要手动 `pip install sglang`。官方的 SGLang wheel 包含无条件的 CUDA 依赖。项目的 `pyproject.toml` 已经通过 `sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'` 做了精妙的条件依赖拦截，自动将 Mac 环境的依赖替换为 `mlx` 和 `mlx-lm`。必须使用 `uv pip install -e .` 让解析器处理这些条件。
FFmpeg 路径硬编码：在 `OmniTyper/backend/server.py` 中，开发者将 `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` 硬编码追加了 `/opt/homebrew/opt/ffmpeg@7/lib`。如果你使用 MacPorts 或没有安装 `ffmpeg@7`，本地启动 OmniTyper 后端时会因为找不到动态链接库而导致音频解码崩溃。

FishAudio 硬件墙：不要在 Mac 上尝试运行 FishAudio S2-Pro。其 `engine_builder.py` 中的 `_resolve_fast_ar_attention_backend` 函数会硬性检测 GPU SM 版本，如果不是 89, 90, 100 或 120，或者找不到 FlashInfer，会直接抛出 RuntimeError，无法通过任何 fallback 绕过。
模型下载超时：`OmniTyper/backend/server.py` 启动时会调用 `snapshot_download` 拉取 `mlx-community/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-4bit` 的特定 revision (`313d850181767edf09f00a9c289becca70e58cd0`)，如果网络环境不佳（如未配置 HF_ENDPOINT），服务启动会长时间假死。

community.process: 1. RFC 先行：重大架构改动或新硬件支持必须先提交带有 `[RFC]` 或 `[Roadmap]` 标签的 Issue 进行讨论（如 Issue 1967, 2052）。2. 代码规范：强制要求在编写或 Review 代码前阅读 `.claude/skills/code-review/coding-style.md`（见 `AGENTS.md` 和 `CLAUDE.md`）。3. 提交前检查：提 PR 前必须在本地运行 `pre-commit run --all-files`（见 `docs/README.md`）。4. 文档规范：优先使用 Markdown，要求相对路径链接，仅在 CI 需要时使用 Notebook。
community.review_style: 极度关注底层性能与工程规范。从大量 `[Runtime Profiling]` 和 `[Perf]` 相关的 Issue/PR（如 PR 2190 packed DiT execution, PR 2225 Reduce AR decode overhead）可以看出，Review 过程会严格审视计算开销、显存占用和调度阻塞问题（如 Commit 144bd63 强调 without blocking the scheduler）。响应速度极快，核心维护者几乎每天都在高频处理 PR。此外，社区对 AI 辅助编程非常友好，专门维护了 `.claude/skills` 目录来对齐 AI Agent 的 Review 标准。
etiquette: 得体：在开发新模型或底层优化前，先开启带有 `[RFC]` 标签的 Issue 与维护者对齐方案。
得体：提交代码前严格执行 `pre-commit`，并遵循 `.claude/skills/code-review/coding-style.md` 中的规范。
得体：在 Apple Silicon 上开发时，复用现有的 MLX/MPS 基础设施（如 `mlx-lm`），并在 PR 中附带本地 Profiling 结果。
不得体：直接提交未经讨论的巨大重构 PR。
不得体：在文档中硬编码绝对链接，或滥用 Jupyter Notebook（除非 CI 强依赖）。
what_they_want: Apple Silicon / MLX 生态建设：这是你最完美的切入点。社区正在大力推进 Mac 本地支持（Issue 1967, 2223），急需精通底层性能的专家来优化 MLX 上的流式 ASR（如修复 Issue 2150 的重复生成 bug）和端侧部署。
DiT 与 TTS 算子级优化：社区正在密集优化 AuK、Qwen3-TTS 等模型（Issue 2064, 1754），并刚合并了 packed DiT execution（PR 2190）。你的 DiT 加速经验可以直接用于减少 AR decode 开销或优化 Flow Matching 阶段。
全双工与流式架构 (Full-Duplex)：社区正在构建实时的语音对话基础设施（Issue 2052, 1909），需要优化跨阶段的调度和显存管理（如 Issue 2236 提到的显存占用释放机制）。
CUDA Graph 与显存复用：虽然你目前受限于 Mac，但你可以参与 `[RFC] Add reusable Prefill CUDA Graph support` (Issue 1357) 的架构设计，利用 Colab T4 进行小规模验证。

entry.ownership_target: Apple Silicon (MLX) 多模态底层性能与 DiT 加速负责人
entry.why_this_target: 首先，这完美契合你的硬件硬约束（只有 MacBook Air），你可以在本地完成 95% 的开发与验证。其次，项目核心维护者 AkazaAkane 正在推进 Apple Silicon 支持路线图 (Issue 1967)，这是一个高优先级且被官方背书的方向。最后，结合你资深的 Kernel 和 DiT 优化背景，你可以直接在 sglang_omni/models/*/mlx/ 目录下产出极具技术深度的代码（如算子融合、显存优化），迅速建立技术威望，从边缘硬件适配者转化为核心性能架构师。

在 Colab T4 上验证并修复旧版 GPU (SM75) 在运行复杂多模态模型时的 Fallback 崩溃问题。

risks.risk: 缺乏高端 GPU 导致无法验证 CUDA Graph、FlashInfer 等核心加速逻辑，可能在修改公共代码时引入 Bug。
risks.mitigation: 严格划定修改范围，优先在独立的 mlx 子目录工作；修改公共调度逻辑时，主动在 PR 中声明“未在 SM90 上验证”，并请求 AkazaAkane 或其他拥有 H100 的维护者协助跑 CI。

risks.risk: 16GB 统一内存在加载多模态大模型（如 Qwen3-Omni + TTS）时极易 OOM，导致本地开发频繁中断。
risks.mitigation: 开发阶段重度依赖 4-bit 量化模型（如 Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-4bit）；在测试 DiT 算子时，编写 Mock 脚本仅加载单层 Transformer Block 的权重进行微基准测试（Micro-benchmarking）。

risks.risk: 项目迭代速度极快（每周/每旬发布），本地分支容易与 main 产生严重冲突。

issues.title: [Feature Request] Support release_memory_occupation / resume_memory_occupation for Omni stages
issues.body:
### Summary

It would be very useful if SGLang-Omni could officially support the upstream SGLang memory-saver lifecycle, including functionality equivalent to:

- `release_memory_occupation`
- `resume_memory_occupation`

for GPU-backed Omni stages such as ASR.

My main use case is `OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`.

---

### Environment

- SGLang-Omni: `0.1.5`
- SGLang: `0.5.19`
- Model: `OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72GB
- Single-GPU deployment
- Docker / SGLang-Omni serving

In my current configuration, the MOSS-TD Omni service keeps roughly **21 GB of VRAM allocated while idle**.

Warm inference is very fast, so restarting the entire Omni service between jobs is not ideal.

---

### Use case

My workload is bursty rather than continuous:

```text
resume / wake MOSS-TD
        ↓
transcribe one long video
        ↓
release GPU memory
        ↓
run other GPU workloads
        ↓
resume MOSS-TD for the next job
````

Other workloads on the same GPU include LLM inference, TTS and audio source separation.

The ideal behavior would therefore be:

```text
SGLang-Omni stays alive
        ↓
MOSS stage enters sleep state
        ↓
weights / KV cache VRAM is released
        ↓
another model can use the GPU
        ↓
resume MOSS stage
        ↓
continue inference without a full cold startup
```

---

### Current behavior

The regular SGLang runtime already contains memory-saver related functionality for:

* `weights`
* `kv_cache`
* `cuda_graph`

and includes APIs / internal implementations around:

```text
release_memory_occupation
resume_memory_occupation
```

However, the SGLang-Omni HTTP server does not currently expose equivalent endpoints.

For example, with a healthy Omni service:

```bash
POST /release_memory_occupation
```

returns:

```text
HTTP 404 Not Found
```

and the same is true for:

```bash
POST /resume_memory_occupation
```

---

### Additional integration issue

I also tried enabling the underlying SGLang memory saver through the Omni engine configuration:

```text
--asr.engine.enable_memory_saver true
```

The option reaches the underlying SGLang model runner, but the ASR stage is spawned by SGLang-Omni's own multiprocessing lifecycle.

This caused the ASR worker to fail during model loading with:

```text
AssertionError: TorchMemorySaver observes invalid LD_PRELOAD.

You can use configure_subprocess() utility, or directly specify
LD_PRELOAD=...

(LD_PRELOAD="" ...)
```

This suggests that Omni's stage worker process is not currently launched under the same memory-saver subprocess configuration used by normal SGLang serving.

I experimented with local monkey patches around the Omni stage spawn path, but this is fragile and version-specific, so official support would be much preferable.

---

### Requested behavior

It would be great if SGLang-Omni officially supported putting selected stages into a GPU memory-saving state.

For example:

```http
POST /release_memory_occupation
```

```json
{
  "stages": ["asr"],
  "tags": ["weights", "kv_cache"]
}
```

and:

```http
POST /resume_memory_occupation
```

```json
{
  "stages": ["asr"],
  "tags": ["weights", "kv_cache"]
}
```

The exact API does not need to match upstream SGLang if an Omni-native admin API is more appropriate.

---

### Desired semantics

Ideally the feature would:

1. Only release memory when the selected stage is idle.
2. Keep the Omni HTTP server and control plane alive.
3. Support releasing at least:

   * model weight

issues.title: [ASR Streaming] Realtime Input Streaming Roadmap and PR Tracker
issues.body:
This is the tracker for **input streaming (live audio in) for ASR models**. New PRs should use the title prefix `[ASR Streaming]` and link this issue in the PR body.

Related trackers: #1267 (ASR refactor, shared mechanics this work builds on), #1754 (TTS roadmap, same tracking format; TTS input streaming is explicitly out of scope there and here).

## Goal

Let clients push audio incrementally over a WebSocket session and receive transcript events while the audio is still arriving, for every ASR model we serve, through **one fixed protocol**. Today `/v1/audio/transcriptions` only accepts a complete file (optionally with SSE output streaming); live captioning, voice agents and telephony need to send audio as it is captured.

## Design principles

1. **Protocol first.** Models adapt to the protocol, not the other way around. A model that can't do something natively declares it; we never bend the wire contract for one model's limitation.
2. **Target OpenAI Realtime GA (transcription intent).** Beta was retired in May 2026 and no current SDK speaks it. The existing `/v1/realtime` conversation session (#385) migrates to GA in the same change.
3. **OpenAI is the baseline, not the whole spec.** Anything it doesn't cover goes in explicit, documented extension fields.
4. **Shared code owns session/transport/events/capabilities; model dirs own encoder feeding and partial/final production.** No model-name branching in shared code (same rule as #1267).

## Requirements gathered from early users

These came from discussions with teams already building streaming STT servers on top of inference backends. They are recorded here in generalized form as design input.

**Transport and audio**
- One WebSocket per stream; PCM16 mono 16 kHz as the default input.
- Audio format is a negotiated session parameter, not a hard constant. Sample rate (8/16/24/48 kHz) and encoding (pcm16, µ-law, A-law) should be declarable; **8 kHz µ-law is a real need for telephony**, not a nice-to-have.
- Deployment topologies to support: co-located (server + model on one GPU box) and split (session/transport layer on CPU, model backend on separate GPUs). The protocol layer must not assume it lives in the same process as the model.

**Capability negotiation**
- On connect / `session.update`, the server declares what the loaded model can actually do, e.g. `partial_style`, `max_decode_window_s`, supported `input_format`s, `languages`, `segmentation_modes`, `concurrency`.
- `session.updated` reports **what was granted**, not an echo of the request. Clients cannot guess per-model behavior from outside, so this is the mechanism that makes "protocol first" work across a heterogeneous model set.

**Partial transcript semantics**
- `partial_style` must be declared explicitly (e.g. `append_only` vs `revising`). Several models (Whisper-style and Qwen3-ASR among them) revise earlier words as more context arrives; treating their output as append-only deltas is silently lossy. Clients need to know whether a delta may replace previously emitted text.

**Long input / buffer limits**
- Buffer overflow must not close the connection (no WS 1009 as the overflow response). A long turn should be split into multiple finals correlated by a turn id, so a session stays alive across arbitrary utterance lengths.

**Division of labour**
- VAD, turn policy, diarization and session admission are per-customer policy and typically live above us; we should make them optional / pluggable, not mandatory.
- What can

issues.title: [Roadmap] Coding Style
issues.body:
## Goal

Gradually bring the main code and tests into alignment with the [code style guide](https://github.com/zhaochenyang20/sglang-diffusion-routing/issues/32), with automated checks for requirements that tooling can express directly.

Start with basic lint checks, introduce type checking to support annotation changes, then expand coverage to tests once the rollout for the main code is established.

## Roadmap

### Phase 1: Coding style guidance and basic Ruff checks

- [x] Establish the initial Ruff configuration, fix existing non-annotation findings outside `tests/`, and enable the checks in pre-commit and CI. #2184
- [x] Add coding style guidance for coding agents and contributors. #2181

### Phase 2: Type checker selection and integration

Ruff can flag missing annotations and some uses of `Any`, but validating annotations against implementations and callers requires a type checker.

- [ ] Evaluate type checkers on representative repository code, considering dependency typing support, diagnostic quality, and incremental adoption.
- [ ] Select a checker and define the initial coverage and strictness, including how untyped dependencies and implicit `Any` are handled.
- [ ] Establish a checked scope in the main code and integrate the check into local development and CI.

### Phase 3: Annotation cleanup in main code

Use the configured type checker to validate annotation changes, migrating module by module.

- [ ] Replace `Any` annotations with types that match the code's actual inputs, outputs, and usage. #2213
- [ ] Add missing parameter and return annotations, and type arguments for bare containers.
- [ ] Resolve type inconsistencies exposed by the checker and review annotation changes against callers.
- [ ] Enable individual Ruff `ANN` rules supported by the guide, including `ANN401`, as the corresponding findings are resolved.

### Phase 4: Extend coverage to tests

Once the checks for the main code are established, apply the same process to `tests/`.

- [ ] Review existing tests against the selected Ruff rules and type checker configuration, including fixture and mock usage.
- [ ] Fix style and annotation findings while preserving test intent and coverage.
- [ ] Gradually include migrated test directories in local and CI checks and remove the current test exclusion.

issues.title: [Tracking] Qwen3-TTS Optimization Follow-Up Roadmap
issues.body:
## Goal

This issue tracks the Qwen3-TTS optimization roadmap. The goal is to improve TTFA, streaming continuity, throughput, and high-concurrency serving efficiency without regressing output quality, deterministic inference, request lifecycle correctness, or streaming behavior.

Related issue: #1418

## Scope

- Qwen3-TTS Base
- Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice
- Talker / Code Predictor
- Reference encoding
- Streaming vocoder / Codec
- CUDA Graph coverage
- Scheduling and batching
- Serving profiles and admission tuning

## Optimization roadmap

### Qwen3-TTS

| PR | Hard / Practical Dependency |
| :--- | :--- |
| **T-PR1** | none |
| **T-PR2** | T-PR1 |
| **T-PR3** | none |
| **T-PR4** | none |
| **T-PR5** | none |
| **T-PR6** | T-PR2 practical dependency, because new chunk shapes need follow-up graph coverage |
| **T-PR7** | none; T-PR2 is only a comparison baseline |
| **T-PR8** | T-PR7 |
| **T-PR9** | T-PR8 + T-PR1 graph lifecycle contract |
| **T-PR10** | early T-PR19 telemetry; T-PR8 + T-PR9 |
| **T-PR11** | bounded response-buffer telemetry from early T-PR19; T-PR10 |
| **T-PR12** | none / parallel track; PR #1643 stacks on #1640 + #1641 |
| **T-PR13** | ideally T-PR6 + T-PR9 + T-PR10 + T-PR11 + T-PR12 |
| **T-PR14** | early T-PR19 admission/queue telemetry; T-PR11; T-PR10 implicitly |
| **T-PR15** | practically T-PR5, though implementation can start independently |
| **T-PR16** | none |
| **T-PR17** | none |
| **T-PR18** | should be after architecture-level optimizations, especially T-PR9–17; otherwise you're optimizing kernels before knowing the remaining bottleneck |
| **T-PR19** | early observability and bounded-delivery slices have no dependency; feature-specific state-slot and graph hardening lands with T-PR8/9/10/11 as applicable + T-PR13 |

#### Planned

- [ ] T-PR11 Feed playback pressure back into Talker scheduling.
  - Add a per-request frames-ahead / buffered-audio high-water mark.
  - Temporarily stop scheduling requests that are sufficiently ahead of playback.
  - Never throttle the initial startup frames required for first audio.
  - Prefer requests that have not emitted their first audio when decode capacity is constrained.
  - Do this through the existing SGLang scheduling path rather than introducing a Qwen3-TTS-specific global four-stage planner.

- [ ] T-PR13 Add production graph-coverage validation and named serving profiles.
  - Add profiles such as:
    - `ttfa`
    - `balanced`
    - `throughput`
  - Profiles should jointly configure:
    - max running / queued requests
    - Talker graph buckets
    - Code Predictor graph buckets
    - Codec chunk schedule
    - Codec graph buckets
    - follow-up batching parameters
    - incremental Codec
    - async decode
    - strict graph fallback policy.
  - Production profiles should validate expected hot shapes during startup instead of silently discovering eager fallback under traffic.

- [ ] T-PR14 Retune Qwen3-TTS admission and concurrency limits after pacing/backpressure is available.
  - Re-evaluate `max_running_requests`.
  - Re-evaluate `max_queued_requests`.
  - Sweep at least c8/c16/c32 and open-loop request rates.
  - Measure realized in-flight requests, queueing time, first-audio latency, throughput, and underruns.
  - Do not raise admission limits independently of downstream playback/backpressure behavior.

#### Active

- [ ] T-PR4 Batch Qwen3-TTS reference encoding and speaker-embedding extraction. PR #1753
  - Reviewed and approved; focused Qwen3-TTS CI enab

issues.title: [RFC][Qwen3-TTS]Serving Adaptation and Optimization
issues.body:
## Motivation

SGLang-Omni already supports voice cloning and streaming generation for Qwen3-TTS-Base. For high-concurrency real-time outbound calling, with target requirements of Mean TTFP `< 800 ms` and Mean RTF `< 0.8`, further work is still needed in production serving APIs, observability, first-packet latency optimization, and the Ascend NPU execution path.

Current benchmark results show that SGLang-Omni provides low RTF, high audio throughput, and stable streaming continuity under high concurrency. However, Mean TTFP exceeds one second starting at concurrency 24, limiting single-instance capacity for real-time outbound calling.

This RFC centrally tracks Qwen3-TTS-Base engineering infrastructure, general performance optimization, and Ascend NPU adaptation. 

Follow-up of #1754 
## Goals
1. Complete the production speech API, including SSE streaming, output sample-rate selection, and token usage.
2. Establish production metrics and benchmark tooling that can locate TTFP, RTF, and streaming continuity bottlenecks.
3. Reduce first-packet latency under high concurrency while preserving RTF and streaming continuity.
4. Complete functional adaptation, graph coverage, and performance tuning for Qwen3-TTS-Base on Ascend NPU.
5. Preserve voice-cloning quality, audio quality, stop semantics, and consistency between streaming and non-streaming output.

The target performance criteria are:

- Mean TTFP `< 800 ms`
- Mean RTF `< 0.8`
- Streaming Continuity OK Rate `≥ 95%`
- Maximize single-instance concurrency while satisfying all the criteria above

### Engineering Infrastructure
- [ ] Add `stream_format="audio" | "sse"` to `/v1/audio/speech`.
  - `audio` continues to return a raw PCM byte stream.
  - `sse` returns `speech.audio.delta`, `speech.audio.done`, and error events.
  - Ensure that the terminal event is emitted exactly once.
  - Reuse the existing disconnect and request-abort handling.

- [ ] Support client-selected output sample rates.
  - Initially support 8 kHz and the native 24 kHz output rate.
  - Perform resampling after vocoder output and before audio encoding.
  - Preserve resampler state across streaming chunks to prevent boundary artifacts.

- [ ] Complete token usage accounting for streaming and non-streaming TTS.
  - Count input text tokens, reference-audio codec frames, and generated-audio codec frames separately.
  - Define `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_tokens`, and input-token details.
  - Expose final usage through non-streaming headers, SSE terminal events, batch results, and WebSocket completion events.
  - Define usage behavior for cache hits, cancellation, generation failures, and output truncation.

- [ ] Provide a production-ready Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint.
  - Request metrics: accepted, rejected, running, waiting, completed, failed, and cancelled requests.
  - Audio metrics: TTFP, RTF, E2E latency, output duration, chunk interval, underrun, and continuity.
  - Stage metrics: preprocessing, Talker prefill, Talker decode, Code2Wav, and inter-process transfer latency.
  - Execution metrics: graph hits, eager fallbacks, cache hits, and NPU operator fallbacks.
  - Aggregate metrics across the API server and stage worker processes.

### Ascend NPU Adaptation
- [ ] Validate model loading and the complete Qwen3-TTS-Base inference pipeline on NPU.
  - Verify that both non-streaming and streaming APIs return audio successfully.

- [ ] Support and validate NPU Graph execution for the Talker stage.
  - Verif

issues.title: [RFC] Full-Duplex Session Infrastructure
issues.body:
## Motivation

Full-duplex interaction can be modeled as a sequence of incremental short requests(Unit). Each unit goes through multiple stages, possibly on different workers. must retain state across units: KV cache, token history, and encoder/codec state. Currently, every request releases its state when it finishes.

This RFC introduce `session`, a long-lived context that holds stage state across units. It is implemented by the realtime layer and the Coordinator on top of the existing pipeline. A session is used to:
- Retain and reuse perception, AR, and codec state across units;
- Handle interruptions at unit boundaries while the session stays open.
- Release resources on close.

## Proposed design

### 1. How state is retained

A session ID will be used to identify long-lived state and each unit is a short request issued under that ID. The Coordinator assigns each stage of a session to a fixed worker, keyed by the session ID, and every unit of that session runs its stages only on those workers. 

When a unit finishes, each stage releases that request's own resources without releasing the session state:
- AR stages reuse SGLang streaming sessions for KV and token history;
- encoder and codec stages keep their own state across units.

### 2. How state is reused

The Coordinator routes each unit by its session ID to the same workers. Units are dispatched one at a time in sequence order. Each unit does incremental computation on the retained state from the previous unit. Overlapping between units is followup optimization.

### 3. How interruptions are handled

The session cancels the current response on an interruption, from the client or from the model, and keeps its state and accepted input. To achieve this, the session keeps an epoch counter. It starts at zero and increases by one on each cancellation. Every unit and its output are assigned the current epoch number. Then:
- The realtime layer drops output whose epoch is behind the counter and tells the client which epoch was cancelled. Based on the information, the client stops and drops audio of the cancelled epoch.
- The Coordinator lets the active unit run to completion to avoid releasing the retained state. After that, the Coordinator and each stage reject any unit that carries the old epoch.

### 4. How resources are released
The session ends on close: 
- The realtime layer stops accepting input, discards queued input that has not been dispatched, and drops any output that still arrives.
- The Coordinator waits for the in-flight unit to complete. After that, it asks each stage to release the session's state. The session's capacity is returned once every stage has confirmed.

## Phase 1 implementation plan

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["Pipeline sessions · #2035"]
    C["AR session bridge · #2069"]
    D["Realtime layer · #2070"]
    P --> C
    P --> D
```
- **Pipeline sessions**: #2035
  - Stage side: add `SessionHooks` (open, append, abort, close) for a stage to keep session state, and `SessionScheduler` to run one unit of a session at a time under capacity limits.
  - Coordinator side: add `CoordinatorSessions` to bind workers by session ID, dispatch units in order, advance the epoch at unit boundaries, and release stages on close.

- **AR session bridge**：#2069
  - Add `ARSessionBridge` in the SGLang backend to map a pipeline session to a SGLang streaming session, so KV and token history stay in the core scheduler across units.

- **Realtime layer**: #2070
  - Add `SessionR

issues.title: [Tracking] MOSS-TTS Optimizations
issues.body:
## Motivation

MOSS-TTS Delay still has significant room for performance improvement. We have implemented a series of optimizations, and this issue tracks their progress as separate PRs.

## Tracking

All items listed below **have already been implemented**. The checkbox tracks whether the corresponding PR has been merged, not whether implementation is complete.

The optimizations are submitted as separate PRs so that each change, performance gain, and quality impact can be reviewed and validated independently.

The performance numbers below come from different points in the development stack. They are useful directional evidence, but they are not cumulative. Each PR will be rerun against its immediate parent before submission.

### Codec ownership and preprocessing

- [x] **Decouple the MOSS-TTS Delay codec and run reference encoding on GPU** — #1222
  - Load the processor with `audio_tokenizer=None` and give preprocessing and vocoder standalone codec ownership.
  - Preserve checkpoint codec metadata, explicit codec overrides, `PathLike` references, and unified path/URL/data-URI audio loading.
  - Rename `codec.py` to `delay_pattern.py` because it contains Delay-pattern logic rather than neural codec execution.
  - Derive the codec device from stage placement while preserving an explicit CPU fallback.
  - Update MOSS-TTS process resource accounting so opt-in stage isolation does not require a manual preprocessing memory-fraction workaround.
  - Full SeedTTS result: `2.9958 -> 4.4395 QPS` (`+48.19%`).

- [x] **Batch and cache reference encoding** — #1348 
  - Route MOSS-TTS Delay reference encoding through the shared `ReferenceEncodeService`, with waveform-content cache identity, same-key single-flight deduplication, byte-bounded LRU caching, and caller-isolated cached tensors.
  - Batch prepared GPU waveforms across different cold references while keeping audio loading and resampling outside the codec worker; retry failed batches per item and close the worker with the preprocessing lifecycle.
  - Five-run full SeedTTS EN result on a single NVIDIA H200 at concurrency 16 (`1088/1088` samples per run): throughput `6.8686 -> 9.0000 QPS` (`+31.03%`); mean latency `2.3228 -> 1.7698 s` (`-23.81%`); P95 latency `2.9000 -> 2.1930 s` (`-24.38%`); mean RTF `0.54038 -> 0.41056` (`-24.02%`).

- [x] **Run MOSS-TTS Local reference encoding on a dedicated CUDA stream** — #2193
  - Give the existing reference encoder worker a persistent CUDA stream, reducing interference with AR generation on reference-cache misses.
  - Establish a one-time dependency on the model-loading stream and complete the CPU-code conversion before resolving each request's future.
  - Five-round full Seed-TTS-Eval EN A/B on one NVIDIA H200 at concurrency 16, with CPU quota limited to 1/8 of the host, 1,088 requests per round, and a fresh server each round. Results use arithmetic means:
    - Local streaming: throughput `12.8234 -> 13.1002 QPS` (`+2.16%`); mean TTFA `326.54 -> 265.84 ms` (`-18.59%`); P95 TTFA `501.44 -> 390.08 ms` (`-22.21%`).

issues.title: [Feature] Bound conversation history growth in `/v1/realtime` sessions
issues.body:
## Motivation `RealtimeSession.conversation` (`sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py`) is an in-memory list that grows without bound for the lifetime of the session: ```python self.conversation: list[ConversationItem] = [] ``` Every turn, `build_response_request` replays the full history into the messages array: ```python for item in self.conversation: messages.append(Message(role=item.role, content=item.text)) ``` There is no client event to delete or compact history. The conversation client-event set is limited to `session.update`, `input_audio_buffer.append`, `input_audio_buffer.clear`, `response.cancel`, and `conversation.item.truncate` — and `truncate` only removes interrupted assistant items from playback bookkeeping. The only bound today is the engine's `context_length`, which surfaces as a hard request failure mid-conversation rather than graceful degradation. For long-lived voice sessions — the primary `/v1/realtime` use case — this is a liveness problem: latency creeps up as prefill grows with each turn, and the session eventually dies at the context limit with no recovery path. The Full Duplex RFC (#2052) explicitly defers "context-usage reporting and compaction" to follow-ups. This issue claims the reporting/bounding half of that follow-up for the turn-based path, which is deployable today and independent of the duplex infrastructure work. ## Proposed design Add a `max_history_turns` (or `max_history_items`) field to `SessionConfig`, settable via `session.update`: - `null` (default): current unbounded behavior preserved. - Positive integer: keep the most recent N turns; drop oldest items on append. - The system `instructions` message is never dropped — it is built fresh each turn and does not live in the list, so this is already safe. - Dropping is applied in `run_turn` after appending the completed user/assistant pair, so a turn in progress is never partially evicted. - The effective bound is reflected in `session.created` / `session.updated` so clients can mirror server-side state. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CL as Client participant SS as RealtimeSession Note over SS: max_history_turns = N (granted at session.update) CL->>SS: input_audio_buffer.append (speech) Note over SS: VAD speech_stopped → auto-commit SS->>SS: run_turn: response + transcription passes SS->>SS: append (user, assistant) pair SS->>SS: while len(conversation) > N: drop oldest SS-->>CL: response.* events (full current-turn reply) Note over SS: next turn's build_response_request replays
at most N turns ``` A token-based bound would be more precise but requires tokenizer access in the session layer. A turn/item-based bound is model-agnostic, trivially testable, and matches the `SessionRuntime` design direction in #2070 (transport-agnostic, typed config). A server-side default cap could follow later as a deployment flag. ## Scope split Two distinct problems share the "history growth" name, and they live on different paths: | Path | Where history lives | Bounding mechanism | Status | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Turn-based sessions (today)** | App-level `conversation` list, replayed into messages each turn | List operation, no engine changes | Deployable now — **this issue** | | **Native duplex sessions (roadmap)** | Retained KV and generated-token history in the core streaming session (#2003 / #2069); the AR bridge appends new input to that history and suppressing output does not remo

issues.title: [RFC] Core AI POC vs MLX-mini on Apple Silicon
issues.body:
## Motivation

show the **Apple Core AI** poc resutls.

[#1967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1967) already tracks first-class Apple Silicon support as **MLX (performance) + Torch/MPS (compatibility)**. Core AI is a third contract: compiled `*.aimodel` bundles, macOS 27+ system runtime, persistent KV inside Core AI, currently batch-one / greedy. It should not be folded into the model-support table in #1967 until we agree on POC scope.

This issue is the place to decide:
1. What a **bounded Core AI POC** looks like (and what it is not).
2. Why the deocode latency can not match our expection

## What we already measured

Public PoC: `adityavaid/sglang` @ `55c8cf4`, model `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.

**M1 Pro 32 GB, macOS 27.0**, 1024-ctx batch=1 median decode step (warmup, then 128 decode tokens):

| Backend | Median decode | tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MLX `mlx_q4` (group 64) | 6.77 ms | ~148 |
| MLX default BF16/fp | 10.89 ms | ~92 |
| Core AI native INT4 | 23.59 ms | ~42 |
| Core AI native FP16 | 26.18 ms | ~38 |


## Proposed POC (bounded)

Treat Core AI as an **experiment + regression sentinel**, not a production Omni backend.

In scope:

- Qwen3-0.6B only, native forward, FP16 and optional INT4 .
- macOS 27 + Apple Silicon gate (`poc.py probe` / specialization).
- Batch=1 1024-ctx per-step decode vs MLX float and `mlx_q4` on the same host.


## Related
@adityavaid Thank you for this Core AI serving PoC, especially the `coreai-opt` authoring path.

- Apple Silicon roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1967
- Hardware reports (optional extra hosts): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/2158

issues.title: Checkpoint path resolution is done differently in every model family
issues.body:
Loading the same repo id costs a different amount of startup time depending on which model family you use, because each family resolves the path its own way:

- six families use the shared `resolve_model_path` — llada2_uni, ming_omni, ming_tts, moss_tts, moss_tts_local, qwen3_omni
- three call `snapshot_download` directly — higgs_tts, and ming_omni / moss_tts in some paths
- about six hand the repo id straight to `from_pretrained` — arkasr, fun_asr, moss_transcribe_diarize, minimax_music3, qwen3_tts, and qwen3_asr until #1808 — which makes every such call re-resolve the repo and ask the Hub whether the cached files moved

The cost is real. On qwen3_asr this pattern was 24 Hub round trips and about 5.6 s of a 12.7 s cold start, with `config.json` revalidated five times; #1808 has the numbers.

No rewrite is needed and nothing breaks. The shared helper already exists, and after #1808 it also refuses to serve an incomplete cache, so every migrated call site inherits that check for free. A migration is a few lines per site and preserves behaviour — the helper returns the same directory the direct call resolves to. Two precedents already exist: #1808 for qwen3_asr's engine builder, and the MLX runner alignment in #1730.

Suggested path: one call site per small PR, each with a cold-start measurement, starting with the ASR families since their startup is what a laptop user waits on. I can send the ones I can test on Apple hardware; the CUDA-only families are one-line changes best done by someone who can run them.

Collaborated with Claude Code.

issues.title: [Feature] Enable torch.compile by default with persistent first-start cache
issues.body:
`torch.compile` is a proven serving optimization in SGLang Omni (lower kernel-launch overhead, fused Inductor/Triton kernels), but it is still opt-in for most models. The usual reason is cold-start cost: the first compile can add tens of seconds before the server accepts traffic.

That cost should be paid **once**, not on every process start. PyTorch already persists compiled artifacts under `~/.cache/torch/inductor` (or `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`). If Omni treats compile + cache as part of the default server lifecycle, later restarts reuse the cache and should not re-pay the compile delay.

Hereby, we wanna to:

1. Turn `torch.compile` on by default for models that already have a supported compile path.
2. On the first `sgl-omni serve` with an empty cache, compile the live graphs and persist the artifacts.
3. Accept a one-time first-start delay of about **60 seconds**.
4. On every later start with a warm cache, skip that delay and serve with compiled kernels immediately.
5. Keep an explicit opt-out (`--enable-torch-compile false` / `engine.enable_torch_compile=false`) for debugging and unsupported backends.

`torch.compile` then becomes a default performance optimization, not a hidden flag that only expert users turn on.

issues.title: [Feasibility] Qualify MOSS-TTS-v1.5 8B on 24/32 GB consumer GPUs
issues.body:
## Goal

Qualify `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS-v1.5` (Qwen3-8B delay-pattern model) on a single 24 GB or 32 GB consumer GPU without publishing an unmeasured low-memory profile.

Parent roadmap: #1120.

## Source-backed memory floor

Pinned public revisions used for this assessment:

- MOSS-TTS-v1.5 `cdd3b911b1585e3f2dbc7775ef10f9926f58850a`: 8,489,841,664 BF16 parameters = **15.81 GiB** of parameter bytes
- MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer `3cd226ba2947efa357ef453bcad111b6eafba782`: 1,774,566,400 FP32 parameters = **6.61 GiB** per copy; BF16 = **3.31 GiB**

Current `main` constructs separate audio-tokenizer models in `create_preprocessing_executor()` and `create_vocoder_executor()`, while all three stages are colocated on GPU 0. The parameter-only GPU floor is therefore:

```
15.81 GiB AR + 6.61 GiB reference encoder + 6.61 GiB vocoder = 29.04 GiB
```

This excludes CUDA context, allocator fragmentation, KV cache, CUDA Graph capture, activations, relay buffers, and generated-code tensors. The current layout is therefore not viable on 24 GB and has no credible runtime margin on a 32 GB RTX 5090.

## Candidate layout to validate

A model-specific low-memory layout can move reference preprocessing to CPU and load the vocoder codec in BF16:

```
GPU parameter floor: 15.81 GiB AR + 3.31 GiB vocoder = 19.12 GiB
CPU parameter floor: 6.61 GiB reference encoder
```

Measured card capacities from the consumer-GPU roadmap artifacts leave, before runtime allocations:

- RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB): **12.72 GiB** above the parameter floor
- RTX 4090 (24,564 MiB): **4.87 GiB** above the parameter floor

These are planning bounds, not startup evidence. The 32 GB layout is plausible at bounded concurrency; the 24 GB layout remains too close to claim without direct measurement and may require CPU vocoding, quantized AR weights, or a shared/offloaded codec design.

## Required implementation ownership

- `sglang_omni/models/moss_tts/`: explicit preprocessing device and vocoder dtype policy; no generic Stage/Scheduler branch
- example config: bounded `max_running_requests`, CUDA Graph cap, and `mem_fraction_static` derived from measured startup
- tests: production config loading and resolved factory args, plus explicit override precedence
- docs: publish only measured capacity and quality results

## Exit criteria

- [ ] Startup on one 32 GB consumer GPU with BF16 AR, CPU reference encoder, and BF16 vocoder
- [ ] Record memory after AR weights, KV allocation, CUDA Graph capture, codec loads, first request, and steady state
- [ ] Validate reference-less and reference-audio requests, streaming and non-streaming output, cancellation, and shutdown cleanup
- [ ] Sweep concurrency and graph caps; report TTFA, RTF, throughput, peak VRAM, host RAM, and power
- [ ] Run SeedTTS EN/ZH quality checks against the existing H200 references
- [ ] Run a sustained mixed-request soak including reference and non-reference traffic
- [ ] Test the same layout directly on 24 GB hardware and publish either a working bounded profile or a measured non-feasibility verdict

## Related work

- #1198 mixed several model fallbacks and carried only unit-level behavior evidence; model-specific work should supersede it
- #1287 covers MOSS-TTS Local (a different 1.7B architecture)
- #1288 covers Voxtral TTS

issues.title: [Roadmap] Prefill/Decode Disaggregation
issues.body:
Design and mechanism co-authored by @MelodyyyYin and me; this issue indexes the work and records the change logs of measurements. The design document behind it is on [Lark](https://ylarkus3pw750a4b.usttp.larksuite.com/wiki/IOkgwbtn2iydAMkRZgnuSI28tob).

## Background

An autoregressive stage does two different jobs. Prefill reads a whole prompt in one step; decode emits one token at a time. Run both on one card and one scheduler thread, and every arriving prompt stalls the tokens already in flight. On Qwen3-Omni that cost is large and it is worst on images, because a 6127-token image prompt cannot be chunked: `_needs_full_prefill` forces the whole prompt through one step, and no decode work batches with it. Measured on one H200, the inter-token gap that overlaps a prefill is 2.28x the gap that does not.

Splitting the two jobs into separate processes is not a new idea, and we are not inventing the pieces. [DistServe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670) made the case that separating them raises goodput per GPU. [Upstream SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) already carries the receiving side: the `PREBUILT` admission path lets a decode engine continue a request whose prompt it never ran, and its [disaggregation code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation) keeps prefix reuse alive on both halves. This repo already carries the transport: paged KV transfer over CUDA IPC landed in #1315 and #1382 with no production consumer, and PD is its first. Stage placement, per-stage processes, and replica binding already exist too. The #1773 implementation uses explicitly declared Prefill and Decode stages and defines the contract that moves a request across their boundary.

What omni adds to the picture is that **the split ratio is not a constant**. A request's prefill share moves with its input. `docs/cookbook/moss_transcribe_diarize.md` profiles a 60-second clip at concurrency 1 with AR decode at 94.0% of total time, and a 5-second clip at concurrency 16 with the encoder at 38.2% and prefill at 29.7%. One prefill worker paired with one decode worker fits one end of that range and strands a GPU at the other. This is why placement here is a continuous parameter rather than a fixed device separation: which devices each half gets, how much of a card each half gets, and eventually how many of each there are. Compare each placement against colocated serving at equal GPU count, with the same workload and CUDA graph settings. Report throughput alongside first-token latency and token gaps; the best placement depends on the workload and its SLO.

## Design responsibilities

The explicit-stage implementation in #1773 uses the responsibilities below. It is under review and has not merged into main.

| Layer | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omni pipeline and runtime | Declared stages, process/replica expansion, placement, routing, completion, abort and health | KV copy protocol, sampling, model execution |
| PD handoff | The typed continuation, transfer identity, replica bindings and source lease | KV copy protocol, decode batching policy |
| CommEngine and transport | Prepare/copy/ACK exchange, transfer cancellation and source-lease lifetime | Continuation contents, sampling, scheduler admission |
| PD schedulers and DecodeKVReceiver | Source mapping export, destination reservation/commit/abort, request reconstruction, `PREBUILT` admission and scheduler-owned cleanup | Any new transport, any model-

issues.title: [Bug] Working Apple SHM setup logs errors for unused Relay dependencies
issues.body:
On a supported native Apple Silicon installation, importing the common Relay API emits ERROR messages for absent Mooncake and NIXL libraries, even though the import and SHM setup succeed. The messages make a working configuration look broken and suggest installing transport packages that it does not need.

## Environment

- Revision: `69ddc6baa9bc5430c0db63bb6fa806b778849b83`
- Hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 32 GB
- macOS 26.5.1; Python 3.12.12; Torch 2.13.0

The project's installation dependency markers deliberately omit the Mooncake/NIXL CUDA packages on macOS arm64, so their absence is expected in this supported configuration.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from the unmodified repository root on that installation. No model, inference service or microphone is needed.

```python
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
from sglang_omni.relay.base import Relay, create_relay

print("base import succeeded")
relay = create_relay("shm", engine_id="probe", device="cpu")
print(type(relay).__name__)
relay.close()
```

Observed output includes:

```text
ERROR:sglang_omni.relay.mooncake:Failed to import mooncake: No module named 'mooncake'. MooncakeRelay will not work. Install with: pip install mooncake-transfer-engine
ERROR:sglang_omni.relay.nixl:Failed to import nixl: No module named 'nixl'. NixlRelay will not work.
base import succeeded
ShmRelay
```

## Actual behavior

The script reaches both print statements and closes the SHM relay normally. The two ERROR messages are emitted during the common import, although the script never selects Mooncake or NIXL. This directs users toward dependencies omitted by the installation configuration and makes genuine configuration failures harder to distinguish.

## Expected behavior

Importing the common Relay API or using SHM in this supported configuration should not emit ERROR solely because unused optional transports are absent. Users should be able to use SHM without installing those CUDA packages.

Explicitly selecting an unavailable backend should still fail clearly and identify the missing dependency.

## Cause

Importing `sglang_omni.relay.base` first executes the Relay package initializer. That initializer eagerly imports the Mooncake and NIXL adapters, whose ImportError handlers log ERROR when their external libraries are absent, before a transport is selected.

issues.title: [Bug from Homebrew] [Apple Silicon]: com.apple.provenance kernel-level content tracking causes portable-ruby 4.0.6 to be SIGKILLed on execution
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On macOS 15 Sequoia, Homebrew's portable-ruby 4.0.6 cannot be installed or executed. After download and extraction, the ruby binary is automatically tagged by the kernel with a new com.apple.provenance extended attribute. When any process attempts to execute this binary, the kernel sends SIGKILL(signal 9) immediately - nodialog, no prompt, no crash log.

This causes install.sh to fail at the verification step(./ruby --version), which rolls back the installation. As a result, every brew command that triggers a portable-ruby upgrade fails, making it impossible to install or upgrade any formula.

Key characteristics of com.apple.provenance:

- **Kernel-protected**: xattr -d, xattr -c, and xattr -w all return Permission denied, even for the file owner. The attribute cannot be modified or removed by user-space tools.

- **Propagates through all file operations**: Copying (cp), redirecting (cat > file), and even base64 round-tripping (base64 | base64 -d) all preserve the provenance attribute on the output file. This indicates kernel-level process/context tracking, not simple filesystem xattr inheritance.

- **Persists across filesystems**: Even when copied to an exFAT volume (which does not support extended attributes natively), the file is still tagged with both com.apple.provenance and com.apple.quarantine, and execution still results in SIGKILL.


### Actual Result
```

issues.title: [Roadmap] Runtime Profile Agent for SGLang Omni
issues.body:
## Goal

Renamed on 2026-09-09 from Kernel Development Agents (KDA) to Runtime Profile Agent. Current scope: profile each model's runtime first, optimize at the scheduling and orchestration layer while the GPU is still idle, and enter kernel work only once the GPU is busy. The kernel stage keeps the adjudication protocol below.

Make agent-driven runtime optimization a repeatable, adjudicated pipeline for SGLang Omni. A generated change is cheap. A trusted change is expensive. The pipeline spends its effort on the second part.

Founding case study: #1608 by @junliu-mde. External references: the [agent assisted SGLang development write-up](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-02-agent-assisted-sglang-development) and [PolyArch humanize](https://github.com/PolyArch/humanize).

## Evaluation protocol (v0, comments welcome)

Every candidate passes the same protocol before any gain is claimed:

1. A correctness gate declared up front: bitwise identity under a controlled batching protocol, or for ASR possibly token identity plus a bounded WER regression, see the open question below.
2. An isolated benchmark against a functionally equivalent baseline under the same inputs, launch path, and compile flags. Control for warm-up and temporal drift, for example interleaved A/B or A-B-A with the first round discarded, and require the effect to clear the measured noise band.
3. Positive evidence the new code path actually executed, from counters or traces. Absence of errors is not evidence.
4. An end-to-end measurement on the target workload. Isolated wins that do not translate end-to-end are retained as optimization inventory but are not counted as delivered gains (#1608 documents this in detail). Match workload size to the effect being measured. In the #1620 reproduction, a 64 sample quick gate could not resolve a c16 effect that a 1088 clip run resolved (see comments). When the noise band is wider than the expected effect, an inconclusive measurement is a rerun trigger rather than evidence of no gain (see finals comment).
5. Independent reproduction before a merge recommendation.

Distilled from #1608, #1418 and the MTD kernel sweep. Corrections welcome, especially from anyone who has hit cases this does not cover.

## Stage 0: calibration (first, about one week)

Run candidate models through tasks with known answers, so the grader is validated against ground truth before we trust it on open problems.

- [x] Main task: reproduce the fused seeded sampling kernel adjudicated in #1608. Network disabled, repository pinned to a fixed commit, graded automatically on the correctness gate and the isolated benchmark.
- [x] Judgment task: predict and explain the end-to-end effect of that kernel. The reference answer is in #1608.
- [x] Finals, top candidates only: reproduce #1620 from its pre-merge base and validate the full chain including end-to-end, since that PR has verified gains of 3.3 to 6.4 percent.

Output per candidate model: pass rate at each gate, accuracy of the end-to-end judgment, and cost per adjudicated task. Plus a grading harness hardened on known answers.

## Stage 1: target qualification
